notes:
T351 (suppress `failed command:` noise from `zig build test`) is STOPPED and reported as a design question, not a code change — per the 2026-08-18 brief-refresh bar: the `[EXPECTED]` and `I4/I5/I7/I9` lines are evidence, and if the only way to satisfy Zig's test runner is to suppress them, stop and report.

FINDING (mechanism, established at Zig 0.16.0 source and by a minimal repro): the cosmetic `failed command:` lines are emitted for any `.zig_test` step whose test binary writes to stderr, even when every test passes and the step exits 0. Chain: `std.debug.print` -> stderr -> `std.Build.Step.Run.evalZigTest` unconditionally sets `run.step.result_stderr` on the success path (Run.zig:1719 `run.step.result_stderr = stderr_owned`) -> `build_runner.zig:1381-1388` calls `printErrorMessages` for ANY step with non-empty `result_stderr` -> `printStepFailure` renders the step as `w` and then prints `failed command: <argv>` (build_runner.zig:1516-1520). The build exit status stays 0 (green); the text just reads red.

THE CONFLICT: the only two output channels a test binary has are stdout and stderr. stdout is the Zig 0.16 test-runner IPC protocol channel (`evalZigTest`/`waitZigTest` read message headers from child stdout, Run.zig:1636-2002) — writing diagnostics there corrupts the protocol; a minimal repro with a flushed stdout write HUNG the runner (bogus header bytes_len -> 60s response-timeout wait). stderr is therefore the only channel that reaches the run log, and stderr is exactly what triggers the cosmetic `failed command:` warning. So bar 1 (zero `failed command:` lines) and bar 5 (keep the `[EXPECTED]`/`I4/I5/I7/I9` evidence in the suite output) are mutually exclusive: eliminating the noise requires suppressing the stderr diagnostics during `zig test` (the `builtin.is_test` / `diag()` gating), which deletes the evidence.

COUNT (cosmetic noise at HEAD, derived from the 2026-08-18 run-2 log `untracked/log/t369-suite-2026-08-18-run2.log` + the deterministic mechanism): 8 cosmetic `failed command:` lines from PASSING test binaries (vb_fixpoint x2, vb_graph x2, vb_closure x1, colex/rules x1, vb_mutants x1, vb_graph mem x1), alongside 6 genuine crash `failed command:` lines and 4 genuine shell-script `failed command:` lines. The noise is therefore real at HEAD and not 'already gone'.

PRIOR WORK REVERTED: the working tree carried an uncommitted partial implementation of the ORIGINAL brief's approach (a `diag()` helper gated on `!builtin.is_test` in all five deliverables). I reverted it to HEAD (`git restore`) because (a) it is exactly the suppression the refresh bar rejects, and (b) it was incomplete (it left rules.zig:562,959-986,1050 and the colex/vb_graph main demo paths ungated). The five source deliverables are now clean at HEAD.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR (design options, not decisions): (1) accept the cosmetic noise — it is already harmless (exit 0) and T369's `tools/suite-truth.sh` gate does NOT parse test-binary `failed command:` lines (it greps only `failed command:.* sh tools/` and `error: '<module>.test.`), so the evidence stays and the gate is unaffected; (2) gate the diagnostics behind an env var (e.g. `WEIZIGO_DIAG=1`) so the default suite is clean and evidence is opt-in; (3) emit evidence to a file + a trailing shell step, an architecture change beyond this row; (4) suppress (`builtin.is_test` gating) accepting the loss of the in-suite evidence, which the refresh explicitly forbids without an Orchestrator decision. claims/new_rows stay empty — tooling/design finding, no epistemic claim touched.
